behavioral_v1.note: The v3 contract defines behavioral-v1 over the same ordered 47 columns as the ML baseline under a separate namespace, so the equivalence classes and counts coincide with ml_feature_equivalent.

duplicates.method: Row-equivalence fingerprints over parsed values using pandas.util.hash_pandas_object (uint64).

duration_throughput.note: Association only. The published feature dictionary does not expose the producer arithmetic, so no causal claim is made.

figures.caption: Counts and shares of the binary `Label` target over every row of the verified source file. The log scale keeps the minority class visible.
figures.title: Binary target distribution (Label)

figures.caption: All ten attack categories with counts and shares. `Worms` is the rarest class; the axis is logarithmic so that rare categories stay readable.
figures.title: Attack category distribution (Attack)

figures.caption: `PROTOCOL` and `L7_PROTO` are numeric-coded categories, not continuous variables. The 15 most frequent codes of each are shown; the full counts are in the machine-readable summary.
figures.title: Numeric-coded protocol distributions

figures.caption: Flow start timestamps grouped per UTC day. The published capture window is a few weeks in 2015; it does not represent contemporary traffic.
figures.title: Capture window coverage per UTC day

figures.caption: Log-transformed flow duration in milliseconds. The distribution is zero-heavy, so the log1p transform is used for readability; no flow is dropped.
figures.title: Flow duration distribution

figures.caption: Inbound/outbound byte and packet counts. Both directions are strongly zero-heavy, which is why a log1p transform is used for the display only.
figures.title: Byte and packet count distributions

figures.caption: Directional average throughput in bytes per second. Non-finite values are not silently replaced; they are counted separately in the population statistics.
figures.title: Average throughput distributions

figures.caption: Joint view of duration and average throughput for rows with finite, non-negative values. The non-finite values of this dataset sit in the rate fields, not in the throughput fields; they are counted in the population contingency table. The association is descriptive and not causal.
figures.title: Duration versus throughput

figures.caption: Pearson correlations restricted to the 37 quantitative baseline features. Numeric-coded categorical fields such as `PROTOCOL` or `TCP_FLAGS` are deliberately excluded.
figures.title: Feature correlation heatmap

figures.caption: Descriptive class-conditional comparison only. These distributions are not used to select features, to tune thresholds or to fit any model.
figures.title: Class-conditional feature distributions

figures.caption: Counts of flows per (zero duration, non-finite rate, non-finite throughput) combination, split by label. The association is an observed property of the published bytes and does not establish how the producer computed the values.
figures.title: Duration and throughput quality contingency

figures.caption: Sample skewness per quantitative feature. Magnitudes above 1 indicate a strongly right-skewed feature and therefore a transformation risk for linear models.
figures.title: Feature skewness

not_permitted_now: Selecting final ML features with held-out or test labels.
Fitting imputers, encoders, scalers or selectors on the full dataset.
Choosing thresholds or hyper-parameters with test information.
Claiming that cross-split leakage has been verified.
Creating an undocumented random split to bypass Issue #7.
Automatic de-duplication or label-dependent row filtering.
permitted_now: Full-dataset source profiling of the verified population.
Data quality audits that do not modify the source bytes.

split_manifest.detail: No verified train/validation/test split manifest exists. Train-dependent analysis must not be performed and no split may be created to bypass Issue #7.

ml_readiness_blockers: raw quality findings require an approved train-only handling policy
real split and leakage audit are NOT VERIFIED (Issue #7)
train-only fitted preprocessing artifact is NOT VERIFIED (Issue #8)

sample.limitations: Sample-based estimates. Full-population counts, means, extremes and complete-case Pearson correlations are computed over every row.
sample.method: reservoir sampling (Algorithm L) over the parsed population
